claims.explanation: Didanosine is a nucleoside analog that, after intracellular phosphorylation, inhibits mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma and is also a substrate for purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP); selectivity likely reflects dependence on purine salvage and mitochondrial DNA maintenance pathways. Lines with intact PNP-mediated purine salvage and high mitochondrial dependence (e.g., high PNP or mitochondrial gene expression) may activate/retain didanosine metabolites and be more sensitive, whereas loss of PNP or impaired nucleoside transport/phosphorylation would be protective. The observed enrichment of TP53 and PI3K/AKT-pathway mutations in sensitive lines is consistent with altered nucleotide metabolism and mitochondrial apoptosis priming rather than a single lineage effect.

features.basis: PNP is the annotated didanosine target and mediates purine analog metabolism
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in selectively killed lines, consistent with impaired DNA damage/mitochondrial apoptosis responses
PIK3CA mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines and may increase nucleotide/mitochondrial dependence
KRAS mutations are common in sensitive lung/colorectal lines and may alter nucleotide metabolism
BRAF mutations appear in sensitive melanoma and colorectal lines
EGFR mutations appear in sensitive NSCLC and esophageal lines
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines and may increase PI3K/mitochondrial dependence
NFE2L2 mutations appear in sensitive esophageal and colorectal lines
ARID1A mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly via chromatin/nucleotide metabolism changes
ATM mutations appear in several least-affected lines, suggesting intact DNA damage response may not be required for resistance
CDKN2A mutations are common in least-affected lines, possibly reflecting reduced proliferation/mitochondrial dependence
NF1 mutations appear in least-affected lines, suggesting RAS/MAPK-independent resistance
